mainTopic: Releasing a vow only בפניו (משה in מדין, צדקיהו and נבוכדנצר), and רבי מאיר's cases that look like a נולד but are not
overview: A ברייתא teaches that when someone is forbidden by a vow from benefiting from another person, the vow may be released only in front of that person (בפניו). רב נחמן finds the source in a פסוק: God told משה in מדין to go back to Egypt, which hints that משה had to release his oath to יתרו there, in front of יתרו. The גמרא then tells how צדקיהו swore to keep נבוכדנצר's embarrassing secret, had the oath released without נבוכדנצר present, and revealed the secret. When נבוכדנצר questioned the סנהדרין, they admitted that such a release must be done בפניו, and they sat on the ground in shame. A new משנה follows. In it, רבי מאיר says that some changes only look like a נולד, such as an evil father who died or did תשובה, or a bad dog that died. The חכמים disagree with him. The גמרא asks how a death could not be a נולד. רב הונא answers that the vow was tied to its stated reason. רבי יוחנן answers that the change had already happened before the vow was made.

steps.title: A vow of benefit is released only in front of the other person
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules that a vow forbidding benefit from a friend can be released only in that friend's presence.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: if someone is forbidden by a vow from getting benefit from his friend, they release the vow for him only in the friend's presence.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא with a new rule about releasing vows. It says the release must happen in front of the person the vow is about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a חכם can release a vow privately with the person who made it. Here there is an extra condition: when the vow involves another person, that person must be present. The rest of this section looks for the source of this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: One forbidden by a vow from benefiting

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule that a release of a vow involving another person needs that person present. The whole section that follows defends this rule.

phrases.english: It was taught: one who is forbidden by a vow from benefiting from his friend
they do not release it for him except in his presence.
phrases.notes: "His presence" means the friend's presence, the person the vow is about.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vow of benefit from another person may be released only in that person's presence.

steps.title: Where do we learn this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the rule that the release must be בפניו.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the ברייתא's rule. This sets up the next step, where an answer will be given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is not obvious from logic alone, so the גמרא wants a פסוק behind it. This is a request for a source, not an attack on the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these matters known? (asking for a source)

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the ruling in Step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for requiring the release to be done בפניו.

steps.title: משה had to release his vow in מדין
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן reads the פסוק where 'ה' spoke to משה in מדין' as telling משה to release his vow there, in front of יתרו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: It is written, 'And ה' said to משה in מדין: Go, return to Egypt, for all the men are dead.' God told him: In מדין you vowed, so go and release your vow in מדין.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers the question with a פסוק. Why does the פסוק say God spoke to משה 'in מדין'? It is hinting that משה had to release his vow in מדין, where יתרו was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra word 'in מדין' teaches that the vow had to be released in the place where it was made, in front of יתרו, the person it concerned. That matches the ברייתא's rule of בפניו.

keyTerms.meaning: In מדין, where משה lived with יתרו

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said: As it is written:
"And the Lord said to Moses in Midian:
Go, return to Egypt,
for all the men are dead."
He said to him: In Midian you vowed;
phrases.notes: משה had promised יתרו he would stay with him, so that promise had to be undone before he could leave.

phrases.english: go and release your vow in Midian.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request for a source in Step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words 'in מדין' teach that משה had to release his vow in front of יתרו, in the place he made it.

steps.title: Proof that משה actually swore to יתרו
steps.stepSummary: The word ויואל is connected to אלה, which means an oath, so משה swore to יתרו.
steps.simpleTranslation: For it is written, 'And משה was willing (ויואל)'. אלה means nothing other than an oath, as it is written, 'And he brought him into an oath (באלה).'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the claim that משה made a vow to יתרו. It shows this from the word 'ויואל' in the פסוק about משה agreeing to stay with יתרו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 3 assumed משה made a vow, but where does it say so? ויואל sounds like אלה, and a פסוק in יחזקאל uses אלה to mean an oath. So משה swore to stay with יתרו.

keyTerms.meaning: And he was willing / agreed (read here as related to אָלָה)

steps.confusionAlert: Step 3 talks about a 'vow' (נדר), and this step proves an 'oath' (שבועה). The גמרא treats them the same for this rule.

phrases.english: As it is written: "And Moses was content"
phrases.notes: שמות 2:21. This is where משה agreed to live with יתרו.

phrases.english: ala means nothing other than an oath,
as it is written: "And he brought him under an oath."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the assumption in Step 3 that משה had vowed to יתרו.
steps.raayaObject: That משה made an oath to יתרו.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The link between ויואל (שמות 2:21) and אלה = oath (יחזקאל 17:13).
steps.whatToRemember: משה swore to יתרו in מדין, so God told him to release it there, in front of יתרו. This is the source for releasing a vow בפניו.

steps.title: How did צדקיהו rebel against נבוכדנצר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק that צדקיהו rebelled against נבוכדנצר, who had made him swear, and asks what the rebellion was.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And he also rebelled against King נבוכדנצר, who had made him swear by God.' What was his rebellion?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new פסוק about צדקיהו and asks what his rebellion was. This sets up a story that will show the rule of בפניו again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links the rebellion to an oath, but it does not say what צדקיהו did. The question opens the story that comes next.

phrases.english: "And he also rebelled against King Nebuchadnezzar,
who had made him swear by God."
phrases.notes: Some versions of the גמרא have the word in round brackets, but the פסוק itself just says "by God," so the corrected wording leaves it out.

phrases.english: What was his rebellion?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a second source, a story, that relates to the rule of Step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What act of rebellion the פסוק is talking about.

steps.title: צדקיהו swears to keep נבוכדנצר's secret
steps.stepSummary: צדקיהו found נבוכדנצר eating a live rabbit, and נבוכדנצר made him swear not to tell anyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: צדקיהו found נבוכדנצר eating a live rabbit. He said to him: Swear to me that you will not reveal this about me and the matter will not get out. He swore.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins answering with a story. נבוכדנצר was caught doing something embarrassing, and he made צדקיהו swear to keep it secret.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the oath the פסוק mentions. Notice the oath was made to נבוכדנצר, so he is the person the oath is about. That will matter for the rule of בפניו.

phrases.english: Zedekiah found Nebuchadnezzar
eating a live rabbit.
He said to him: Swear to me
that you will not reveal this about me
and the matter will not get out. He swore.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of Step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: צדקיהו swore to נבוכדנצר to keep his embarrassing secret.

steps.title: צדקיהו has his oath released and tells the secret
steps.stepSummary: צדקיהו suffered from keeping the secret, had his oath released, and revealed it. נבוכדנצר summoned the סנהדרין and צדקיהו to complain.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end צדקיהו was suffering in his body. He asked for release from his oath and told. נבוכדנצר heard that people were mocking him. He sent for the סנהדרין and צדקיהו and said to them: Do you see what צדקיהו has done? Didn't he swear by the name of Heaven that 'I will not reveal'? The reply was: He asked for release from the oath.
steps.whatsHappening: The story goes on: צדקיהו had his oath released, without נבוכדנצר there, and spread the secret. נבוכדנצר confronts the סנהדרין, and they explain that the oath was released.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the 'rebellion': צדקיהו broke his word to נבוכדנצר. The key detail is that the release happened while נבוכדנצר was not present, which sets up the question about בפניו.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked for release (from a חכם)

phrases.aramaic: לְסוֹף הֲוָה קָא מִצְטַעַר צִדְקִיָּהוּ בְּגוּפֵיהּ.
phrases.english: In the end, Zedekiah was suffering in his body.
He asked for release from his oath, and told.
Nebuchadnezzar heard that they were mocking him,
he sent for and brought the Sanhedrin and Zedekiah.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוֹן: חֲזֵיתוּן מַאי קָא עָבֵיד צִדְקִיָּהוּ?
phrases.english: He said to them: Do you see what Zedekiah has done?

phrases.aramaic: לָאו הָכִי אִישְׁתְּבַע בִּשְׁמָא דִשְׁמַיָּא דְּ״לָא מְגַלֵּינָא״?
phrases.english: Did he not swear this way by the name of Heaven, "I will not reveal"?
The reply was: He asked for release from the oath.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְסוֹף הֲוָה קָא מִצְטַעַר צִדְקִיָּהוּ בְּגוּפֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story and shows how צדקיהו broke his oath.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: צדקיהו's oath was released without נבוכדנצר present, and he revealed the secret.

steps.title: The סנהדרין admit the release must be בפניו
steps.stepSummary: נבוכדנצר asks if oaths can be released and whether it must be in the other person's presence. The סנהדרין answer 'בפניו', and he asks why they did not tell צדקיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Can one ask for release from an oath? They said: Yes. He said: In his presence, or even not in his presence? They said: In his presence. He said: And you, what did you do? Why did you not tell צדקיהו?
steps.whatsHappening: נבוכדנצר questions the סנהדרין about the law. They admit that an oath like this may be released only in front of the person it concerns, and he blames them for not saying so.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is where the story supports the ברייתא: the סנהדרין themselves state that the release must be בפניו. Since נבוכדנצר was not there, the release of צדקיהו's oath was not proper.
steps.whyThisMatters: The story confirms the rule of Step 1 from the mouths of the סנהדרין: an oath made to someone is released only in his presence.

phrases.english: He said to them: Can one ask for release from an oath?
phrases.notes: Not every version has the words in square brackets; they're added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: They said to him: Yes.
He said to them: In his presence,
or even not in his presence?
They said to him: In his presence.
He said to them: And you, what did you do?
Why did you not tell Zedekiah?
phrases.notes: He means: why didn't you tell him he could only be released with me there?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: בְּפָנָיו, אוֹ אֲפִילּוּ שֶׁלֹּא בְּפָנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the release described in Step 7 broke the rule of בפניו.
steps.raayaObject: The rule of Step 1 that release must be done בפניו.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The סנהדרין's own answer to נבוכדנצר: 'בפניו'.

steps.title: The elders sit on the ground in shame
steps.stepSummary: The elders had no answer and fulfilled the פסוק 'They sit on the ground in silence'. רבי יצחק explains they pulled the cushions out from under themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: Immediately, 'The elders of the daughter of ציון sit on the ground and are silent.' רבי יצחק said: They removed the cushions from under themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with the סנהדרין silent and ashamed. רבי יצחק explains that 'sitting on the ground' means they took away their cushions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their silence shows they knew they had made a mistake by releasing the oath without נבוכדנצר there. This closes the story and supports the ברייתא's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The elders of the daughter of ציון

steps.whatToRemember: Two sources back the rule that an oath or vow involving another person is released only בפניו: משה releasing his oath in מדין, and the סנהדרין's mistake with צדקיהו.

phrases.english: Immediately, "They sit on the ground and are silent,
the elders of the daughter of Zion."

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: שֶׁשָּׁמְטוּ כָּרִים מִתַּחְתֵּיהֶם.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzḥak said: That they removed the cushions from under them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the סנהדרין's reaction to נבוכדנצר's question in Step 8.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The סנהדרין admitted their error by their silence, which confirms that the release had to be done בפניו.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: Some things look new but are not
steps.stepSummary: The משנה opens with רבי מאיר's rule that some changes look like a נולד but are not really one, and the חכמים disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: רבי מאיר says: There are things that look like a new situation but are not a new situation, and the חכמים do not agree with him.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. רבי מאיר states a general rule, and the משנה tells us right away that the חכמים argue with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a נולד, something new that happened after the vow, cannot be used to release a vow. רבי מאיר says certain changes only look new, so they can still be used. The examples come in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מַתְנִיתִין, 'our משנה'. It marks the start of a משנה.
Literally 'born'. A new situation that came up after the vow was made.
Things that look like a new situation.
The חכמים do not agree with him.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
Rabbi Meir says:
There are matters that are like a new situation
phrases.notes: A 'new situation' here means something that changed after the vow was made.

phrases.english: but are not like a new situation,
and the Rabbis do not agree with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: יֵשׁ דְּבָרִים שֶׁהֵן כַּנּוֹלָד וְאֵינָן כַּנּוֹלָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story of צדקיהו and opens a new משנה about releasing vows.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, some changes only look like a נולד and may be used to release a vow. The חכמים disagree.

steps.title: Examples: the evil father, the bad dog, the snake
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives examples of רבי מאיר's rule: an evil father who died or did תשובה, and a dog or snake that died.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? He said, 'קונם, that I marry so-and-so, because her father is evil,' and they told him the father died or did תשובה. Or, 'קונם, this house that I enter, because a bad dog is inside,' or 'because a snake is inside,' and they told him the dog died or the snake was killed. These look like a new situation but are not. And the חכמים do not agree with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks 'how so?' and gives real cases to explain רבי מאיר's rule. It ends by repeating that the חכמים disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In each case the man said why he was making the vow, and later that reason went away. רבי מאיר says this change does not count as a true new situation, so it can be used to release the vow. The חכמים say it is a new situation.

keyTerms.meaning: A vow word. It makes something forbidden, like a קָרְבָּן.

steps.confusionAlert: Why רבי מאיר says these cases are 'not like a נולד' is not explained in the משנה. The גמרא gives two answers: רב הונא says the vow was tied to its stated reason (Step 13), and רבי יוחנן says the change had already happened before the vow (Step 14).

phrases.english: How so?
He said: "Konam, that I marry so-and-so,"
phrases.notes: He means: marrying her is forbidden to me with a vow.

phrases.english: "because her father is evil,"

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: מֵת, אוֹ שֶׁעָשָׂה תְּשׁוּבָה.
phrases.english: they told him: he died, or he repented.
"Konam, this house that I enter,"
"because a bad dog is inside it,"
or "because the snake is inside it,"
they told him: the dog died,
or the snake was killed —
these are like a new situation, yet it is not like a new situation.
And the Rabbis do not agree with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיצַד? אָמַר ״קֻוֽנָּם שֶׁאֲנִי נוֹשֵׂא אֶת פְּלוֹנִית, שֶׁאָבִיהָ רַע״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the examples for רבי מאיר's general rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the stated reason for the vow goes away (the father dies or does תשובה, or the dog or snake dies), רבי מאיר says this is not a true נולד. The חכמים disagree.
steps.whatToRemember: In every case of the משנה, the man gave a reason for his vow, and that reason later went away.

steps.title: But death is surely a new situation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the dog case and asks how the dog's death could not be a נולד.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: "קונם, that I enter this house because the dog, etc." Death is a new situation!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי מאיר. If the dog died after the vow, that sounds like the clearest new situation there is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attack is on רבי מאיר's claim that this is 'not like a נולד'. A death after the vow is something that really changed, so why should it not count as new?

keyTerms.meaning: Short for גְּמָרָא. It marks the start of the גמרא.
Etc. The rest of the quote is known.

phrases.english: Gemara:
"Konam, that I enter this house
because the dog, etc." —
Death is a new situation!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the dog example from the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's claim that the dog's death is not a נולד.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A death after the vow is a real change, so it should count as a new situation.

steps.title: רב הונא: The vow was tied to its reason
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that by giving a reason, the man made his vow depend on that reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: He is considered like one who hangs his vow on a condition.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers the question. He says the man's vow was tied to his reason from the very beginning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the man said 'because the dog is there', his vow really means 'as long as the dog is there'. When the dog dies, the vow falls away by itself, so we do not need to treat the death as a new reason to release it.

keyTerms.meaning: Hangs his vow on something. The vow depends on a condition.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
He becomes like one who hangs his vow on a matter.
phrases.notes: He means: it is as if he said 'I won't enter as long as the dog is alive.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: נַעֲשָׂה כְּתוֹלֶה נִדְרוֹ בְּדָבָר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dog's death is a new situation used to release a vow that still stands.
steps.terutzMaskana: The vow was tied to the dog all along, so it ends when the dog dies.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: It had already happened before the vow
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that they tell him the father had already died or done תשובה before he made the vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: They are telling him, 'He had already died,' or 'He had already repented.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a different answer. The משנה is not talking about a change after the vow at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יוחנן, the death or the תשובה happened before the vow. So the man made his vow based on a mistake, and nothing new came up after the vow. That is why it is 'not like a נולד'.

keyTerms.meaning: He had already died, before the vow was made.

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא says the vow was tied to a condition that ended. רבי יוחנן says the change happened before the vow, so the vow was a mistake from the start.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
He already died, or he already repented,
phrases.notes: 'Already' means before the man ever made his vow.

phrases.english: is what they are telling him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: כְּבָר מֵת וּכְבָר עָשָׂה תְּשׁוּבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to the same question as רב הונא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changes the timing of the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The death or תשובה happened after the vow.
steps.terutzMaskana: It happened before the vow, so nothing is new. The vow was made by mistake.
